Findings:
↑Sepsis
Enterobacteriaceae abundance >5% was associated with increased sepsis risk (HR 6.577; 95% CI 2.246-19.255; p = 0.021).

↑All-cause mortality
Lachnospiraceae abundance ≤10% was associated with increased all-cause mortality (HR 4.439; 95% CI 2.181-9.035; p < 0.001).
↑Infection-related mortality
Lachnospiraceae abundance ≤10% was associated with increased infection-related mortality (HR 7.051; 95% CI 2.007-24.778; p = 0.006).
↑Non-infection-related mortality
Lachnospiraceae abundance ≤10% was associated with increased non-infection-related mortality (HR 21.211; 95% CI 4.949-90.915; p < 0.001).

↑Non-infection-related mortality
Enteric colonization by Gram-negative MDR was associated with increased non-infection-related mortality (HR 10.280; 95% CI 1.536-68.795; p = 0.048).

↓aGvHD
Higher relative abundance of Blautia was protective against subsequent aGvHD development (p < 0.05).

↓aGvHD
When compared to patients who developed GvHD, individuals without aGvHD showed a higher relative abundance of Blautia (mainly Blautia wexlerae) (8.7% vs. 4.0% [skin GvHD] vs. 1.4% [gut GvHD]; p = 0.046). Blautia negative association with aGvHD was confirmed by Random Forest analysis (p = 0.046)

↓aGvHD
Higher relative abundance of Ruminococcus was protective against subsequent aGvHD development (p < 0.05).
